_note: English text for guide/en/ and the English recommended map. Keyed by the id in spots.json. Only the fields that have text in spots.json. 'hana' = Hana's comments in the same order (comment, then more[]). Translated 2026-11-14 from the Japanese; if the Japanese changes, update here. Missing ids/fields fall back to the Japanese text on the page. Never add the A-tei address or coordinates.

urari_marche.name: Urari Marche (Fish Hall & Vegetable Hall)
urari_marche.note: A direct-sales market: fish on the 1st floor, Miura vegetables on the 2nd. Tuna offcuts, grilled seafood, street food. Also the base for the ferry, sightseeing boats, and rental bikes
urari_marche.hours: Fish Hall 9:00–17:00 (Sun from 7:00) / Vegetable Hall 10:00–17:00 (Sat, Sun & holidays from 9:00) *to be confirmed
urari_marche.closed_note: The building is open every day. Each shop has its own days off (Tue, Wed, etc.)

misaki_asaichi.name: Misaki Morning Market
misaki_asaichi.note: A market held only on Sunday mornings. Tuna offcuts, dried fish, and Miura vegetables. It peaks at 7:00, so go early
misaki_asaichi.closed_note: Closed over New Year (12/29–1/10; year-end special sale on 12/29–30)
misaki_asaichi.price: Free entry. Shinko parking: 2-hour free ticket during the market

jogashima_osakana.name: Jogashima Osakana Market
jogashima_osakana.note: A fresh-fish shop opened in April 2026 (Keikyu Group). Fish landed at Jogashima and Misaki, processed foods, and souvenirs
jogashima_osakana.closed_note: When Tuesday is a holiday, closed the next day
jogashima_osakana.access: 1 min walk from the “Jogashima Gyoko-mae” bus stop. Also close if you cross to the island by ferry

shirokuma.name: Misaki no Shirokuma (shaved-ice café MiX)
shirokuma.note: Shaved ice all year round. Seasonal “Shirokuma” flavors (grape, ohagi, chocolate mint…) are the specialty
shirokuma.closed_note: Closed Thu & Fri (to be confirmed). Was temporarily closed 9/28–10/2

kurobatei.name: Kurobatei
kurobatei.note: A tuna restaurant listed in the tourist association's food guide (Misaki old town)
hana: There's an ADDress set meal just for ADDress members!

uoichiba_shokudo.name: Misaki Fish Market Diner
uoichiba_shokudo.note: A diner at the fish market, listed in the tourist association's food guide. Hours and days off not yet checked

misaki_donuts.name: Misaki Donuts (main shop)
misaki_donuts.note: An old-town doughnut shop listed in the tourist association's food & souvenir guide
misaki_donuts.closed_note: Wednesdays (also temporary closures, e.g. New Year)
hana: A bit pricier than Mister Donut, lol, but I always look forward to the seasonal doughnuts!

miura_brewery.name: Miura Brewery
miura_brewery.note: Local craft beer, listed in the tourist association's food & souvenir guide. Hours and days off not yet checked

jogashima_park.name: Jogashima Park (Kanagawa Prefecture)
jogashima_park.note: Clifftop paths with views of the sea and Mt. Fuji. 300,000 double-flowered daffodils from mid-January to mid-February. Two stars in the Michelin Green Guide
jogashima_park.access: From Misakiguchi Station stop No. 2, bus for Jogashima about 30 min to “Hakushu-hi-mae”, then 5 min walk

jogashima_lighthouse.name: Jogashima Lighthouse
jogashima_lighthouse.note: Designed by French engineer Verny in 1870; the fifth Western-style lighthouse lit in Japan. Shops and rocky shore at its foot
jogashima_lighthouse.access: 5 min walk from the “Jogashima” bus stop

umanose.name: Umanose Sea Arch
umanose.note: A sea arch carved by waves. The ground is rough, so wear good shoes. Walking on top of the arch is prohibited (risk of collapse). No toilets
umanose.access: 15 min walk from “Hakushu-hi-mae” bus stop / 25 min from “Jogashima”. Reachable from both the park side and the lighthouse side

jogashima_bridge.name: Jogashima Bridge
jogashima_bridge.note: 575 m long; you can walk across. Boso Peninsula to the east, Izu Oshima to the south, Mt. Fuji to the west. The bridge glows at dusk. In early May and mid-August, “Diamond Fuji” (sun setting on Fuji's peak) can be seen from the bridge
jogashima_bridge.price: Free (on foot, by bike, by car)

koajiro.name: Koajiro Forest
koajiro.note: A 1.6 km boardwalk running from forest to tidal flats to the sea. About 1 hour from the Hikihashi entrance. Long sleeves and long pants recommended. No pets or bicycles
koajiro.closed_note: Fully closed until the end of November due to typhoon damage (prefecture notice, as of 2026-10-05)
koajiro.access: Bus from Misakiguchi Station about 4 min to “Hikihashi”, then 5 min walk. No parking

kainan.name: Kainan Shrine
kainan.note: Founded in 982; the guardian shrine of Misaki. Prayers for safety at sea, good catches, and business. Home of the July summer festival and the November masked dances (men-kagura). A short walk from A-tei

aburatsubo.name: Aburatsubo Bay
aburatsubo.note: A quiet, winding bay chosen as one of Kanagawa's 50 scenic spots. Yacht harbor at the back and the ruins of Arai Castle. Swimming beaches at Araihama and Yokobori in summer
aburatsubo.price: Free (city parking, 102 spaces, 520 yen per entry, 8:30–17:00)

awasaki.name: Awasaki Lighthouse
awasaki.note: A lighthouse at the eastern tip of Jogashima Park; the end of the park's walking path

miura_beach.name: Miura Kaigan Beach
miura_beach.note: The largest sandy beach on the Miura Peninsula. Swimming in summer; walks and sunsets the rest of the year. Tourist info center and rental bikes in front of the station

sanshiro.name: Sanshiro Ferry (Misaki ⇔ Jogashima)
sanshiro.note: A small ferry between Urari and Jogashima. Bicycles ride free, and pets are OK (on a leash)
sanshiro.closed_note: Closed on Tuesdays from September 2026 (except holidays). The tourist association page still says “open every day”, so be careful
sanshiro.price: Adults 500 yen, elementary students 300 yen. 1-day pass: adults 1,000 yen

nijiiro.name: Nijiiro Sakana-go underwater sightseeing boat
nijiiro.note: A semi-submersible boat. It passes under Jogashima Bridge to an underwater viewing area. You can feed the fish and seagulls
nijiiro.hours: 9:20–16:00, 7 trips a day (8 in summer). Tickets on sale from 9:00
nijiiro.closed_note: Open every day (check in bad weather)
nijiiro.price: Adults 1,700 yen, elementary students 800 yen, preschoolers 200 yen

js_fishing.name: J's Fishing (Jogashima sea fishing pond)
js_fishing.note: Fishing in floating sea pens, no gear needed. Reservation required (phone 046-854-9891 or web)
js_fishing.price: 1-hour trial from 3,000 yen; 1-hour unlimited fishing from 5,500 yen (plus tax)

mikan.name: Miura mandarin picking
mikan.note: 9 orchards in the city (Kamimiyada, Kikuna, Kaneda, Wada). The thing to do at A-tei in autumn; easy to stop by on your way home
mikan.price: Elementary age and up 1,200 yen, preschoolers 900 yen, age 2 and under free (includes about 1 kg to take home)
mikan.access: The tourist info centers in front of Misakiguchi or Miura-Kaigan Station guide you to an orchard. No reservation needed (groups of 20+ must book)

otb.name: KEIKYU OPEN TOP BUS MIURA
otb.note: An open-top double-decker bus. You can also ride with the voucher in the Misaki Maguro Kippu ticket
otb.closed_note: No service on the 2nd Wednesday of each month (inspection). May not run in rain or bad weather
otb.price: One way 1,500 yen, loop 2,000 yen (digital discounts available)

maholova.name: Maholova Minds Miura day-trip bath
maholova.note: Hot-spring bath at a hotel near the station. A soak after a day by the sea
maholova.price: 1,300 yen (same price for elementary age and up; preschoolers free). Towels extra
maholova.access: 7 min walk from Miura-Kaigan Station; free shuttle

misaki_shitamachi.name: Misaki Shitamachi shopping street
misaki_shitamachi.note: The old town where A-tei is. The tourist association's souvenir list includes Uoto main shop, Shimasei (sweets), Marusei noodles, Mitomi dye works, Yajirushi shop, Kurobatei workshop, and more. Night market in October and the mikoshi parade

keikyu_bus.name: Keikyu Bus (Misakiguchi Sta. ⇔ Misaki Port / Jogashima)
keikyu_bus.note: From Misakiguchi Station to Misaki Port, the nearest stop to A-tei, take the bus. The bus for Jogashima crosses the bridge to the island
keikyu_bus.access: From Misakiguchi Station stop No. 2: buses for “Misaki-ko”, “Jogashima”, or “Toriya”. For A-tei, get off at “Misaki-ko”. Fares and timetables: Keikyu Bus official site

rentacycle.name: Miura Rent-a-Cycle (e-bikes)
rentacycle.note: One-way returns OK at Misakiguchi Station, Urari, Jogashima, Miura-Kaigan Station, and Soleil Hill. Book on the web (with the Misaki Maguro Kippu, go directly)
rentacycle.hours: Urari 9:00–17:00 (Misakiguchi and Miura-Kaigan stations 9:30–17:00; Jogashima returns only 9:00–16:00)
rentacycle.price: E-bike 1,000 yen for 3 hours, 1,800 yen per day. One-way fee 600 yen

umikaze.name: Umikaze Cycle (road & cross bikes)
umikaze.note: For riders going around the peninsula. Kids' bikes too
umikaze.price: Cross bike 2,500 yen for 3 hours, e-cross bike 1,800 yen, road bike 4,300 yen

parking.name: Parking (Urari, Misaki fishing port, Jogashima)
parking.note: For guests with a car. On Jogashima, a One-Day Pass lets you use the island's parking lots freely
parking.hours: Urari, Misaki Fishing Port Plaza, and Shinko: 24 hours. Jogashima Park: 8:00–17:00 (Apr–Sep until 19:00)
parking.price: Urari 240 yen/hour, max 700 yen for 12 hours / Misaki Fishing Port Plaza 210 yen/hour / Jogashima Park 500 yen/day (One-Day Pass)

tourist_info.name: Misakiguchi Station Tourist Information
tourist_info.note: English-speaking staff. Rental bike pick-up and return, and mandarin-picking information
tourist_info.closed_note: Open every day except over New Year

hospital.name: Miura City Hospital
hospital.note: An emergency-designated hospital (accepts emergency patients). Phone 046-882-2111. Check consultation hours with the hospital

emergency.name: In an emergency (110 / 119)
emergency.note: Ambulance or fire: 119. Crime or accident: 110. Give A-tei's address (it is in the email from the day before your stay)

hazard.name: Tsunami and disasters
hazard.note: Miura City's hazard maps for tsunami, storm surge, and landslides (city website, in Japanese). If you feel strong shaking, go to high ground

kinoyo.name: Kinoyo (tuna dishes & sushi, Misaki)
kinoyo.note: A tuna and sushi restaurant founded in the Meiji era. Its signature is the “Torotoro-don”, a bowl topped with four kinds of tuna. Tatami seating; no cards
kinoyo.closed_note: Closed Tuesdays (Monday evenings closed). May close around 18:30 when sold out
kinoyo.access: Walking distance from the Misaki-ko bus stop
hana: Hana loves the Torotoro-don! It's topped with tuna in lots of different flavors!

misakikan.name: Misakikan Honten
misakikan.note: A ryotei inn founded in 1908; said to be the first in Japan to serve grilled tuna head (kabuto-yaki). Overlooks the port

shichibeemaru.name: Maguro Shokudo Shichibeemaru
shichibeemaru.note: A tuna and seafood-bowl diner. Open straight through the day; 40 seats over 3 floors. Cards and e-payments accepted
shichibeemaru.closed_note: Closed only on New Year's Day

maruichi_shokudo.name: Misaki Maruichi Shokudo
maruichi_shokudo.note: A diner that cooks fish from the Maruichi fish shop next door as sashimi, salt-grilled, or simmered. Set meals and platters
maruichi_shokudo.hours: 11:00–16:00 (tourist association) / LO 16:00, Sat, Sun & holidays LO 16:30 (Rurubu)
maruichi_shokudo.closed_note: Sources differ (tourist association: irregular, sometimes closed Tue–Wed / Rurubu: Wednesdays)
maruichi_shokudo.access: 3 min walk from the Misaki-ko bus stop

sakinoya.name: Sakinoya
sakinoya.note: A sushi restaurant: nigiri, bowls, and courses. Seafood bowl and the chef's-choice sushi course are classics. About 65 seats, tatami room upstairs. Reservations by phone 046-881-3266
sakinoya.closed_note: Closed Mondays (Tuesday if Monday is a holiday)

senmiraku.name: Senmiraku
senmiraku.note: A tuna restaurant run by a tuna wholesaler founded over 80 years ago. Sushi, sashimi, and bowls. Cards accepted
senmiraku.closed_note: Closed Tuesdays (open on holidays), plus irregular days
senmiraku.access: About 2 min walk from the port

waraya.name: Maguro no Warayakiya
waraya.note: A specialty restaurant serving Misaki Port tuna seared over burning straw. Wheelchair accessible, menus in other languages, parking for 2–3 cars
waraya.access: 5 min walk from the Misaki-ko bus stop

kura.name: Japanese restaurant Misakiko Kura
kura.note: A Japanese restaurant that will cook fish you caught. Seafood bowls, sea bream tempura. 35 seats, parking available

marutsune.name: Marutsune
marutsune.note: A sushi restaurant for tuna and local fish. Counter and tatami seating. Reservations recommended (046-802-0241)
marutsune.access: A little away from Misaki Port

korakutei.name: Korakutei
korakutei.note: Home of Misaki tuna ramen. Chinese food. Cards and QR payments accepted
korakutei.hours: Mon–Fri 11:30–15:00 (LO 14:00) / Sat & Sun 11:30–15:00, 17:30–21:00 (LO 20:00). Closes when the soup runs out
hana: Noodles in thick sauce (ankake soba)
My sister-in-law works here! Mapo ramen, motsu-ni (offal stew) ramen! The fried chicken is delicious! The daily lunch is recommended too!

bocca.name: Misaki Italiano Bocca
bocca.note: A seafood Italian restaurant on the 2nd floor overlooking the port. Courses available. Parking discount at the nearby Misaki Port Exchange Plaza
bocca.hours: Wed–Sun 11:30–15:00, 18:00–22:00 (one listing says lunch only on Fri)
bocca.access: 1 min walk from the Misaki-ko bus stop
hana: Tasty Italian
Everything is delicious! Lunch is great value! It's run by a married couple, so if the service feels off, they probably just had a fight, lol

suzumeya.name: Kissa & Zakka Suzumeya
suzumeya.note: A small 16-seat café. Banana milkshake, firm custard pudding, French toast. The 2nd-floor window seats look over the port. No parking
suzumeya.access: Right by the Misaki-ko bus stop

caba.name: caba coffee beans
caba.note: A small specialty-coffee roastery. Beans sold online too

bread3204.name: 3204 bread&gelato
bread3204.note: Bread and gelato (opened May 2022). Takeout available

misakipresso.name: Misakipresso
misakipresso.note: A café and bar for coffee and drinks. No food these days (as of Nov 2026). 10 seats, parking available
misakipresso.price: coffee 450–500 yen, beer 700 yen, wine 650 yen
hana: A café where you can watch the Kamome Choir practice! Lucky if you catch one of their occasional shared-kitchen days

shokubomiura.name: Shokubo miura
shokubomiura.note: An izakaya serving fish from the Miura Peninsula. Fried horse mackerel, sashimi, pickles, curry. Tatami and sunken-kotatsu seating, parking available
hana: Just delicious! The tomato salad is outstanding! Carefully made food and drinks — very satisfying!

mezcal_love.name: Mezcal Love
mezcal_love.note: Mezcal and Mexican food. Opened at Misaki Port in November 2020

sxs.name: SxS (S by S)
sxs.note: Poke bowls with Miura ingredients (4 kinds), tuna curry, pasta, crêpes. No parking
sxs.access: 5 min walk from the Jogashima bus stop

keikyu_store_higashioka.name: Keikyu Store Misaki Higashioka
keikyu_store_higashioka.note: A Keikyu-group supermarket (the one called “Keikyu Store Misaki”)
keikyu_store_higashioka.access: About 20 min by Keikyu bus from Misakiguchi Station; right by the “Misaki Higashioka” stop

fuji_super_misaki.name: Fuji Super Misaki
fuji_super_misaki.note: A local supermarket open until 22:00. Parking; e-money accepted

megumi_chokubai.name: Misaki Megumi Suisan (tuna wholesaler shop)
megumi_chokubai.note: A tuna wholesaler's direct-sales shop. Offcuts and rare cuts. Parking for 2 cars

minato_uotonya.name: Minato Uotonya
minato_uotonya.note: A Misaki tuna wholesaler. Sells vacuum-packed small portions. Also online sales and hometown-tax gifts

maguro_chokuhan.name: Maguro Chokuhan Center (Kanagawa Fisheries Federation)
maguro_chokuhan.note: Sells tuna and Miura Peninsula seafood on the grounds of the prefecture's largest tuna processing plant

ishii_shoten.name: Ishii Shoten (turban shells & abalone)
ishii_shoten.note: A shop for turban shells (sazae) and abalone from the Miura Peninsula and Odawara
ishii_shoten.closed_note: Closed only on New Year's Day

coin_laundry_misakiyo.name: Coin Laundry Depot Miura Koyo
coin_laundry_misakiyo.access: About 41 min walk (about 3.3 km) from Misakiguchi Station

yatai_misaki.name: Yatai (izakaya)
yatai_misaki.note: An izakaya serving oden, tuna monja, and okonomiyaki. Tatami seats with griddles, and a street-stall-style counter
yatai_misaki.price: 2,000–3,000 yen per person (Google Maps user reports)
hana: Oden, okonomiyaki
Oden and okonomiyaki! Lots of à la carte dishes too! When the owner is on their own, the food comes out slowly!

daiki_sakanatosakana.name: Sakana to Sakana Daiki
daiki_sakanatosakana.note: A Japanese izakaya in a back alley of Misaki Port. Misaki Port fish and local vegetables served as sashimi, salt-grilled, or simmered (opened December 2024)
hana: The wife catches the fish and squid, the husband serves them! Not just seafood — a big menu, recommended!

chochin_tokyo_1.name: Chochin Tokyo No. 1 (Gohan to Osake)
chochin_tokyo_1.note: An izakaya at Misaki Port in a former snack bar. Skewers, abura soba, cold noodles, and more (opened December 2022; “No. 1” is in the name)
hana: It feels like a late-night place, but it opens early too! The multinational-style food might get you hooked!

otoyu.name: Izakaya Otoyu
otoyu.note: An izakaya down an alley off the Misaki Shitamachi shopping street. Famous for fish dishes by an owner who used to cook for tuna fishing boats (24 seats)
hana: Everything is good!
An old-style izakaya run by a family! Reliably delicious!

keimaru.name: Osakana Kobo Keimaru
keimaru.note: A tuna and fresh-fish shop in Misaki 2-chome. Tabelog reviews describe it as a fisherman's direct shop with rare tuna cuts and delicacies
hana: If you're buying tuna, this is the place!
Their tuna is the best! You'll be amazed by the price too! But it's so unpredictable that it's never open when I go, lol. If you want some, ask Hana!

tabegotoya_minato.name: Tabegotoya Minato
tabegotoya_minato.note: Home-style cooking with an Asian touch, using Miura Peninsula ingredients. Bento and deli at lunchtime (opened May 2022, run by two sisters)
hana: Asian; bento on weekday lunchtimes
Hana recommends the peanut noodles! Run by two lovely sisters!

misaki_lumiere.name: Misaki Lumière
misaki_lumiere.note: A curry & bar in Misaki. Curry from 1,000 yen. Also serves “Danchone”, a sausage made from tuna tail meat (500 yen each)
misaki_lumiere.hours: 15:00–24:00 (on Sundays also at the Misaki Morning Market, from opening to 8:30)
misaki_lumiere.closed_note: Closed Tue–Sat. Irregular days off too. Details on the shop's Instagram
hana: Spice curry

chuka_botan.name: Chinese restaurant Botan
chuka_botan.note: A long-standing local Chinese diner in Misaki with over 70 years of history. Popular for handmade jumbo shumai and wonton noodles with charcoal-grilled char siu
hana: Tasty Chinese, shumai
Everything is delicious at this neighborhood Chinese place! The shumai is outstanding!

kinmedai_koukai.name: Kinmedai specialty restaurant Koukai
kinmedai_koukai.note: Specializes in kinmedai (golden-eye snapper): marinated kinmedai bowl, simmered and grilled fish set meals, sashimi set meal, salty fish-bone soup. Fillets and miso-marinated fish sold at the shop front
kinmedai_koukai.hours: Weekdays 11:00–15:00 / Sat, Sun & holidays 10:30–15:30 (dinner by reservation 18:00–20:00, courses from 5,000 yen)
kinmedai_koukai.closed_note: Mondays, and one Tuesday a month (see Instagram)
hana: Kinmedai
Misaki isn't just tuna — there are kinmedai boats too, so you can eat a fresh kinmedai set meal!

sushi_ohata.name: Sushi Ohata
sushi_ohata.note: A sushi restaurant opened by Ohata Sengyo, a fresh-fish shop at Misaki Port. Opened August 2026. Opens early on Sunday morning-market days
hana: The limited lunch is recommended too! Please try the kinmedai tempura!

asameshi_arube.name: Asameshi Arube
asameshi_arube.note: A breakfast place near the Misaki-ko bus stop. Breakfast with Miura vegetables and local ingredients. Different pop-up shops take turns by day (run by MISAKI STAYLE)
hana: Breakfast
Little side dishes you think you could make at home but never do! Dried fish from a local shop! A breakfast that warms your heart — recommended!

watatsumi_misaki.name: Misaki Maguro to Shun no Sakana Watatsumi
watatsumi_misaki.note: A seafood restaurant one street behind, directly opposite Urari at Misaki Port. Misaki tuna and seasonal fish (30 seats, tatami room upstairs)
hana: My daughter works part-time here! Reasonable prices but amazing! Fresh! Highly recommended! Good for sake lovers too!

joshuya_curry_yakiudon.name: Joshuya
joshuya_curry_yakiudon.note: A diner in Tenjin-cho, Miura City. Famous for curry yaki-udon (around 1,000 yen per reviews). 13 seats
hana: Yaki-udon
Misaki's soul food! Curry yaki-udon is the most popular, but Hana can't eat spicy food, so I have the regular yaki-udon!

ichigoichie.name: Shokudoraku Ichigo Ichie
ichigoichie.note: A set-meal diner and izakaya in Shiroyama-cho, Miura City (north of Misaki Port). Tuna and local fish, sashimi platters, seafood bowls
hana: Cheap! Delicious! Can't believe you can eat this well for this price!

ryoushigoya.name: Ryoshi Goya
ryoushigoya.note: A seafood restaurant (Google Maps category). Misaki 1-chome
hana: The fried chicken is a must! Highly recommended! It's unpredictable whether it's open, but lately it's been open short hours on weekends!

yaoshige.name: Yaoshige
yaoshige.note: A greengrocer with homemade deli dishes and bento (Google Maps reviews)
hana: Bento
Sometimes they put out discounted vegetables and fruit, so I dash over! Lots of lunch bento choices, but they're on the sweet side!
